talks.title: The Next Medium: Why Real-Time Interactive Video Changes Everything

sessions.scheduled_title: The Next Medium: Why Real-Time Interactive Video Changes Everything for Developers

positions.claim: World models should be defined as real-time interactive video, not as Gaussian splatting or offline video generation.
Real-time generation changes the nature of the medium rather than only making existing workflows faster.
Uber could not have existed without GPS, and Instagram and TikTok could not have existed without real-time visual feedback while shooting.
The main unmet need of content creators using generative video is control, not output quality.
Instant feedback is the highest attainable form of control, and it is unreachable without real-time generation.
Once real-time generative advertising works, pre-produced ads will no longer be needed; brand risk aversion is what delays this, not capability.
The future of education is neither LLM-based nor textbook-based but situated, steppable simulated experiences.
Robotics world models are already a very large market, with many labs training such models.
Interactive avatars remain unsolved and still feel off in customer support deployments.
Current real-time video editing platforms built on these models are not yet good, limited by model quality.
Batch inference infrastructure cannot be reused for real-time inference; streaming, live-session memory, and global compute are new requirements.
Real-time interactive video requires sub-100ms latency everywhere, which forces geographically distributed GPU capacity.
Memory is a current failure mode of live world models — Genie 3 demos show characters forgetting scenes when they look away and back.
Raising real-time frame rates from 16 FPS to 30 FPS is achievable today via multi-GPU serving, weight optimization, and quantization; it is a prioritization question.
No one, including DeepMind, has solved evaluation of consistency in real-time world models; the field relies on human eyeballing.
The right layer for a startup here is the developer platform and infrastructure, letting the community build deterministic rule-checking and higher-level tooling on top.
